intervals.label: KASCADE-Grande operation
intervals.note: "KASCADE-Grande has started combined data acquisition with all detector components since the end of 2003." End: "stopped finally the active data acquisition of all its components ... end of 2012" (Haungs et al., arXiv:1504.06696). The December 2003 to March 2009 range quoted is the span of the analysed data set; operation continued to the end of 2012.
intervals.quote: The data presented here were taken from December 2003 to March 2009

intervals.label: data acquisition stopped
intervals.note: Start is the month the paper gives ("end of 2012").
intervals.quote: KASCADE and its extension KASCADE-Grande stopped finally the active data acquisition of all its components including the radio EAS experiment LOPES end of 2012 after more than 20 years of data taking

quantity.quote: consists of the Grande array with 37 stations of 10 m2 scintillation detectors each
spread over an area of 700 × 700 m2

lineage.note: KASCADE-Grande is described as an extension of KASCADE, reusing its detectors.
lineage.quote: As an extension of the former KASCADE experiment running successfully since 1996, KASCADE-Grande was built by reassembling 37 stations of the former EAS-TOP experiment

website.quote: KASCADE - Grande The KASCADE-Grande Experiment at KIT Campus North

name: KASCADE-Grande
notes: Placed at the existing campus-grade site:kit-campus-north (see experiment:kascade).
The 37 Grande stations were reassembled from the EAS-TOP experiment at Campo Imperatore (running 1987-2000 per the KASCADE-Grande page); EAS-TOP is not recorded here.
The Tunka-Grande array of TAIGA is built from former KASCADE-Grande scintillators (TAIGA lecture).

physics_goals.quote: KASCADE – Grande was an extensive air shower experiment array to study the cosmic ray primary composition and the hadronic interactions in the energy range E0=1016-1018eV
physics_goals.value: Study the cosmic-ray primary composition and the hadronic interactions between 10¹⁶ and 10¹⁸ eV.

summary.plain: KASCADE-Grande stretched the KASCADE array to 0.5 square kilometres with 37 scintillator stations recycled from an Italian experiment. It found a second, "heavy" knee in the cosmic-ray spectrum near 80 PeV.
summary.technical: Extension of KASCADE by the 37-station Grande array (10 m2 scintillators, 700 m × 700 m, stations reassembled from EAS-TOP), joint operation with KASCADE detectors and LOPES radio antennas from December 2003 to the end of 2012; covers 1016-1018 eV. Observed a steepening of the heavy-primary spectrum at about 8 × 10¹⁶ eV.
